title: TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile (UEFI)
description: The default: PCR use defined by the TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile for UEFI firmware, as implemented by EDK II. PCRs 8-15 belong to the operating system.

registers.long: SRTM, BIOS, host platform extensions, embedded option ROMs and PI drivers: the S-CRTM version, the platform firmware volumes, optional SRTM contents (e.g. Boot Guard ACM, key manifest, boot policy manifest), non-host code and information, integrated option ROMs.
Boot#### and BootOrder variables, filtered SMBIOS tables, multiprocessor information on servers, entering setup, non-host configuration, OEM setup variables and policy, possibly microcode.
Third-party UEFI drivers such as option ROMs on add-in cards, drivers from unmeasured firmware volumes, updatable non-host code, SPDM firmware blobs.
Configuration and data of the drivers in PCR 2: entering setup, non-host configuration, SPDM firmware configuration, third-party setup settings.

title: Linux on UEFI (shim, GRUB, systemd, IMA)
description: PCRs 0-7 as in the TCG scheme, with what shim, GRUB, systemd-boot and systemd-stub add, and PCRs 8-15 as used by GRUB, IMA, systemd and shim, from the Linux TPM PCR Registry (UAPI.7).

registers.long: Core system firmware code (as in the TCG scheme); systemd-pcrosseparator extends a separator barrier at the end of boot.
Host platform configuration data such as serial and model numbers; systemd-stub measures SMBIOS types 1, 2 and 11 when it starts.
Extended or pluggable executable code, including option ROMs.
Data about pluggable hardware.

The boot loader, extra drivers and binaries it loads; shim measures the PE binary it chain-loads; the Linux kernel when booted as a UEFI PE binary; systemd-stub measures system extension images read from the ESP.
The GPT/partition table; systemd-boot measures its loader.conf.
Platform manufacturer specific; on Linux only the systemd-pcrosseparator barrier.
Secure Boot state and certificate updates; shim measures most non-MOK certificates and its SBAT data.
GRUB: every command executed (also from its configuration files), the kernel command line and module command lines.
GRUB: every file read, including the kernel image; the Linux kernel measures initrds passed with the LOAD_FILE2 protocol.
The Linux Integrity Measurement Architecture: protects the IMA measurement log.
systemd-stub: the components of a unified kernel image (UKI); systemd-pcrphase: the boot phase milestone strings.
systemd-stub: a manually specified kernel command line, credentials, configuration images and add-ons; systemd-boot: the kernel command line.
systemd-stub: system extension images passed to the initrd.
shim: the Machine Owner Key certificates and hashes (MokList, MokListX, MokSBState).

registers.short: Machine, disk and file system identity
registers.long: systemd-cryptsetup: the root volume encryption key (optional); systemd-pcrmachine: the machine ID; systemd-pcrfs: mount points, UUIDs and labels of / and /var.
Debug use; resettable.

title: Intel TDX measurement registers
description: The measurement registers of an Intel TDX trust domain (TD), reported in the TD quote. With TDVF (OVMF), the TCG PCRs map to them: PCR 0 to MRTD, PCRs 1 and 7 to RTMR0, PCRs 2-6 to RTMR1, PCRs 8-15 to RTMR2.

registers.long: Measurement of the initial contents of the TD (the TD's firmware image, e.g. TDVF), set at build time.
Run-time extendable register 0: with TDVF the TD's configuration and firmware data (TCG PCRs 1 and 7: configuration, Secure Boot policy).
Run-time extendable register 1: with TDVF the boot loader and other boot applications (TCG PCRs 2-6).
Run-time extendable register 2: the operating system (TCG PCRs 8-15), e.g. the kernel command line and initrd.
Run-time extendable register 3: not used by the firmware; for the guest's own (application or runtime) measurements.
Software-defined ID for non-owner-defined configuration of the TD, e.g. OS or runtime settings (48 bytes, set at TD creation).
Software-defined ID for the TD's owner (48 bytes, set at TD creation).
Software-defined ID for owner-defined configuration, e.g. workload-specific settings (48 bytes, set at TD creation).

title: Arm CCA realm measurements
description: The measurements of an Arm Confidential Compute Architecture realm, reported in the realm token (IETF draft-ffm-rats-cca-token).

registers.long: The compound extension of the measurements of realm memory and state taken before the realm is activated.
Extended by realm guest software at run time (e.g. firmware).
Extended by realm guest software at run time.
Extended by realm guest software at run time.
Extended by realm guest software at run time.
64-byte value given at realm creation, distinguishing realms with the same initial measurement.

title: AMD SEV-SNP attestation report
description: The measurement fields of an AMD SEV-SNP guest attestation report (SEV Secure Nested Paging Firmware ABI Specification). SNP itself has no run-time extendable registers; a vTPM in the guest (e.g. via an SVSM) can provide PCRs.

registers.long: The launch digest: measurement of the guest's initial memory and state (e.g. OVMF, kernel, initrd, command line with measured direct boot).
32 bytes supplied by the host at launch, e.g. a policy or configuration hash.
Digest of the ID key that signed the guest's ID block.
Digest of the author key that signed the ID key, if any.
64 bytes supplied by the guest when requesting the report, e.g. a nonce or key hash.

title: Intel SGX enclave identity
description: The identity measurements of an Intel SGX enclave, reported in its report and quote.

registers.long: Measurement of the enclave's code and data as it was built and loaded.
Hash of the public key of the enclave's signer (the sealing authority).

title: AWS Nitro Enclaves PCRs
description: The PCRs (SHA-384) of an AWS Nitro enclave, reported in its attestation document. Enclaves in debug mode report all zeros.

registers.long: Contiguous measure of the contents of the enclave image file, without the section data.
Contiguous measurement of the kernel and boot ramfs data.
Contiguous, in-order measurement of the user applications, without the boot ramfs.

registers.short: IAM role of the parent instance
registers.long: Measurement of the IAM role assigned to the parent instance.
Measurement of the ID of the parent instance.
Measure of the signing certificate of the enclave image file (signed images only).
